knitr::opts_chunk$set(

*This page is a benchmark of the method. To use repdist on your own data, start with [Get started](vignette.html).*

**Question.** When the proteins of one function share less than 30% sequence
identity, do `repdist` bins recover the function as one unit, and does that
help differential abundance and beta diversity? Baselines: proteins,
MMseqs2 30% clusters, and the COG label itself (an oracle).

```{r libs}
library(repdist)
library(vegan)
```

# Data

`curated/simulation_kofam.rds`, built by `data-raw/simulation_kofam.R` from
the NCBI COG 2024 release [@galperin2025cog]: proteins with exactly one COG,
assigned over their full length (membership class 0), 50-1000 aa, one per
unique sequence. One COG is the treatment; the background is other COGs,
minus any protein with an MMseqs2 hit (E $\le$ 10^-3^, 80% coverage of both)
to a treatment protein [@steinegger2017mmseqs2]. Embeddings are TM-Vec
[@hamamsy2024tmvec]; the similarity graph is `protein_similarity()` at its
defaults, computed at build time.

```{r data}
sim_path <- file.path("curated", "simulation_kofam.rds")
have_sim <- file.exists(sim_path)
if (have_sim) {
    kf <- readRDS(sim_path)
    ann <- kf$annotation
    proteins <- kf$proteins
    smoke <- isTRUE(kf$provenance$smoke)
} else {
    smoke <- NA
}
have_sim
```

```{r smoke-banner, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
if (!have_sim) {
    cat("> **No `curated/simulation_kofam.rds` found.** Result chunks are",
        "skipped; see `data-raw/README.md` for the build command.\n")
} else if (isTRUE(smoke)) {
    cat("> **`KOFAM_SMOKE=1` build.** Tens of proteins with random",
        "unit-vector embeddings: a pipeline check. Every number below is",
        "computed, but none of it is a result.\n")
}
```

```{r universe, eval = have_sim}
treat <- ann$role == "treatment"
data.frame(treatment = kf$design$treatment_cog, name = ann$cog_name[treat][1],
    proteins = nrow(ann), treatment_proteins = sum(treat),
    treatment_30pct_clusters = length(unique(ann$mmseqs30[treat])),
    background_COGs = length(unique(ann$cog[!treat])))
```

How common is this regime? The share of same-COG protein pairs with no
MMseqs2 alignment of $\ge$ 30% identity over 80% of both proteins:

```{r regime, eval = have_sim}
h <- kf$mmseqs$hits
close <- with(h[h$id30_cov80, ], c(paste(p1, p2), paste(p2, p1)))
beyond <- function(ids) {
    pr <- utils::combn(ids, 2)
    mean(!paste(pr[1, ], pr[2, ]) %in% close)
}
bg <- split(ann$protein[!treat], ann$cog[!treat])
bg_beyond <- vapply(bg[lengths(bg) >= 2L], beyond, 1)
c(treatment = beyond(ann$protein[treat]), background_median = median(bg_beyond),
    background_q25 = unname(quantile(bg_beyond, 0.25)),
    background_q75 = unname(quantile(bg_beyond, 0.75)))
```

# Bins against the labels

Pairwise recall (share of same-COG pairs in one unit) and purity (share of
same-unit pairs that share a COG), for the treatment COG and for all COGs.

```{r bins, eval = have_sim}
n <- length(proteins)
S <- matrix(0, n, n, dimnames = list(names(proteins), names(proteins)))
S[cbind(kf$similarity$i, kf$similarity$j)] <- kf$similarity$s
S <- S + t(S)
diag(S) <- 1
bins <- bin_proteins(S)
cog <- setNames(ann$cog, ann$protein)
mm30 <- setNames(ann$mmseqs30, ann$protein)
tc <- kf$design$treatment_cog
pair_scores <- function(unit) {
    tab <- table(unit[ann$protein], cog[ann$protein])
    ch <- function(k) k * (k - 1) / 2
    a <- rowSums(tab)
    t_in <- tab[, tc]
    c(`treatment recall` = sum(ch(t_in)) / ch(sum(t_in)),
        `treatment purity` = sum(ch(t_in)) / sum(ch(a) - ch(a - t_in)),
        `units holding treatment` = sum(t_in > 0),
        `all-COG recall` = sum(ch(tab)) / sum(ch(colSums(tab))),
        `all-COG purity` = sum(ch(tab)) / sum(ch(a)))
}
knitr::kable(rbind(bins = pair_scores(bins$membership), `MMseqs2 30%` = pair_scores(mm30)),
    digits = 3)
```

# Count model

The negative-binomial model of the earlier simulations: depth $D = 2 \times
10^4$, size factor $s_i \sim \mathrm{LogNormal}(0, 0.25)$, log-normal baseline
$\pi$, dispersion $\phi_{ij} = (0.1 + 1/\mu_{ij})\, e_j$ with $e_j \sim
\mathrm{LogNormal}(0, 0.5)$. Each condition-A sample puts a share $\rho$ of
its abundance on `r if (have_sim) kf$design$n_enriched` treatment proteins,
each from an MMseqs2 30% cluster that no other sample uses (a fresh draw per
replicate); condition B has $\rho = 0$. So no sequence family is enriched in
more than one sample, while the function is enriched in every A sample.

```{r count-model, eval = have_sim}
depth <- 2e4
treat_ids <- ann$protein[treat]
draw_enriched <- function(n_per_group) {
    k <- kf$design$n_enriched
    cl <- unique(mm30[treat_ids])
    cl <- cl[sample.int(length(cl), k * n_per_group)]
    p <- vapply(cl, function(c) {
        m <- treat_ids[mm30[treat_ids] == c]
        m[sample.int(length(m), 1L)]
    }, "")
    unname(split(p, rep(seq_len(n_per_group), each = k)))
}
simulate <- function(seed, rho, n_per_group) {
    set.seed(seed)
    ids <- ann$protein
    up <- draw_enriched(n_per_group)
    samples <- sprintf("s%02d", seq_len(2 * n_per_group))
    pi <- rlnorm(length(ids))
    pi <- pi / sum(pi)
    s <- rlnorm(length(samples), 0, 0.25)
    e <- rlnorm(length(ids), 0, 0.5)
    p <- matrix(pi, length(samples), length(ids), byrow = TRUE,
        dimnames = list(samples, ids))
    p[seq_len(n_per_group), ] <- (1 - rho) * p[seq_len(n_per_group), ]
    for (j in seq_len(n_per_group)) {
        p[j, up[[j]]] <- p[j, up[[j]]] + rho / length(up[[j]])
    }
    mu <- s * depth * p
    phi <- (0.1 + 1 / mu) * rep(e, each = length(samples))
    list(counts = matrix(rnbinom(length(mu), mu = mu, size = 1 / phi),
            length(samples), dimnames = dimnames(p)),
        group = factor(rep(c("A", "B"), each = n_per_group)),
        enriched = unlist(up))
}
rhos <- c(0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05)
n_grid <- if (isTRUE(smoke)) 4L else c(10L, 20L)
n_rep <- if (isTRUE(smoke)) 2L else 50L
```

$\rho \in \{0, 1\%, 2\%, 5\%\}$, $n \in$ `r if (have_sim) paste(n_grid, collapse = ", ")`
per condition, `r if (have_sim) n_rep` replicates, the same seed at every
$\rho$ for one replicate.

# Differential abundance and beta diversity

Counts are summed per unit (protein, MMseqs2 30% cluster, `bin_glom()` bin,
or COG) and tested with DESeq2 [@love2014deseq2] as in the
[case study](case_study.html#differential-abundance): `~ group`,
`poscounts`, Wald, adjusted p $\le$ 0.05. A call is a true positive if the
unit holds an enriched protein and most of its abundance is on treatment-COG
proteins. Power: share of replicates with a true positive; Type I: share of
$\rho = 0$ replicates with any call; FDR: share of calls at $\rho > 0$ that
are not true positives. Beta diversity: PERMANOVA [@anderson2001permanova;
@oksanen2025vegan] (999 permutations) on MMD [@gretton2012mmd] and on
Bray-Curtis over proteins and over MMseqs2 30% clusters.

```{r helpers, eval = have_sim}
da_call <- function(agg, group) {
    agg <- agg[, colSums(agg) > 0, drop = FALSE]
    dds <- function() DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(round(t(agg)),
        data.frame(group = group), ~ group)
    fit <- function(...) DESeq2::DESeq(dds(), sfType = "poscounts", quiet = TRUE, ...)
    # Small (smoke) universes can fail both dispersion fits; then use the
    # gene-wise estimates as final, as DESeq2's own message suggests.
    gene_wise <- function() {
        d <- DESeq2::estimateSizeFactors(dds(), type = "poscounts")
        d <- DESeq2::estimateDispersionsGeneEst(d)
        DESeq2::dispersions(d) <- S4Vectors::mcols(d)$dispGeneEst
        DESeq2::nbinomWaldTest(d, quiet = TRUE)
    }
    d <- tryCatch(fit(), error = function(e) tryCatch(fit(fitType = "mean"),
        error = function(e2) gene_wise()))
    r <- DESeq2::results(d, contrast = c("group", "A", "B"), alpha = 0.05)
    setNames(!is.na(r$padj) & r$padj <= 0.05, colnames(agg))
}
glom <- function(counts, m) t(rowsum(t(counts), m[colnames(counts)]))
units <- list(protein = setNames(ann$protein, ann$protein), `MMseqs2 30%` = mm30,
    bin = bins$membership, `COG (oracle)` = cog)
one_replicate <- function(sim) {
    tot <- colSums(sim$counts)
    da <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(units), function(u) {
        m <- units[[u]]
        agg <- if (u == "bin") bin_glom(sim$counts, bins) else glom(sim$counts, m)
        called <- da_call(agg, sim$group)
        share <- tapply(tot * treat, m[names(tot)], sum) / tapply(tot, m[names(tot)], sum)
        hit <- names(called) %in% m[sim$enriched]
        tp <- called & hit & share[names(called)] > 0.5
        data.frame(level = u, called = sum(called), tp = sum(tp))
    }))
    rel <- sim$counts / rowSums(sim$counts)
    d <- list(MMD = sample_mmd(rel, proteins),
        `Bray-Curtis, proteins` = vegdist(rel, "bray"),
        `Bray-Curtis, MMseqs2 30%` = vegdist(glom(rel, mm30), "bray"))
    beta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(d), function(k) {
        set.seed(1)
        a <- adonis2(d[[k]] ~ group, data = data.frame(group = sim$group), permutations = 999)
        data.frame(distance = k, R2 = a$R2[1], p = a$`Pr(>F)`[1])
    }))
    list(da = da, beta = beta)
}
```

```{r grid, eval = have_sim}
t0 <- Sys.time()
grid <- expand.grid(replicate = seq_len(n_rep), rho = rhos, n = n_grid)
runs <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(g) {
    r <- one_replicate(simulate(grid$replicate[g], grid$rho[g], grid$n[g]))
    list(da = cbind(grid[g, ], r$da, row.names = NULL),
        beta = cbind(grid[g, ], r$beta, row.names = NULL))
})
da <- do.call(rbind, lapply(runs, `[[`, "da"))
beta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(runs, `[[`, "beta"))
knit_minutes <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))
```

```{r da-table, eval = have_sim}
wide <- function(d, key, stat) {
    out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d[key], drop = TRUE), function(x) {
        v <- vapply(rhos, function(r) stat(x[x$rho == r, ], r), 1)
        data.frame(x[1, key, drop = FALSE], t(setNames(v, paste0("rho=", rhos))),
            check.names = FALSE)
    }))
    rownames(out) <- NULL
    out
}
da_stat <- function(x, r) if (r == 0) mean(x$called > 0) else mean(x$tp > 0)
fdr <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(da)), da[c("level", "n")], function(i) {
    i <- i[da$rho[i] > 0]
    if (sum(da$called[i])) 1 - sum(da$tp[i]) / sum(da$called[i]) else NA
})
da_tab <- wide(da, c("level", "n"), da_stat)
da_tab$`FDR (rho>0)` <- fdr[cbind(da_tab$level, as.character(da_tab$n))]
knitr::kable(da_tab, digits = 2, caption = paste("Differential abundance:",
    "the rho=0 column is Type I, the others power"))
```

```{r beta-table, eval = have_sim}
knitr::kable(wide(beta, c("distance", "n"), function(x, r) mean(x$p <= 0.05)),
    digits = 2, caption = "PERMANOVA (p <= 0.05): the rho=0 column is Type I, the others power")
```

# Summary

```{r summary-values, include = FALSE}
if (have_sim) {
    sc <- rbind(bins = pair_scores(bins$membership), mm = pair_scores(mm30))
    pw <- function(l, r) da_tab[da_tab$level == l & da_tab$n == n_grid[1], paste0("rho=", r)]
}
```

- **Regime.** `r if (have_sim) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * beyond(ann$protein[treat]))`
  of treatment-COG pairs are beyond 30% identity (background COGs: median
  `r if (have_sim) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * median(bg_beyond))`).
- **Bins.** Treatment recall `r if (have_sim) sprintf("%.2f", sc["bins", 1])`
  for bins vs `r if (have_sim) sprintf("%.2f", sc["mm", 1])` for MMseqs2 30%,
  at purity `r if (have_sim) sprintf("%.2f", sc["bins", 2])` vs
  `r if (have_sim) sprintf("%.2f", sc["mm", 2])`.
- **Differential abundance** at $\rho$ = 2%, $n$ = `r if (have_sim) n_grid[1]`:
  power `r if (have_sim) sprintf("%.2f", pw("bin", 0.02))` for bins,
  `r if (have_sim) sprintf("%.2f", pw("MMseqs2 30%", 0.02))` for MMseqs2 30%,
  `r if (have_sim) sprintf("%.2f", pw("protein", 0.02))` for proteins and
  `r if (have_sim) sprintf("%.2f", pw("COG (oracle)", 0.02))` for the COG oracle.
